original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On the selected PR1094 gauge44 provider, fuse only four consecutive events with child ranks (2,2,1,1) in any order into one rank-6 block-diagonal child. Enumerate every eligible window and maximum disjoint schedule in both complete orientations, then apply the exact zero-additional-cost local ceiling screen.
scope_change_reason: The broad rank-shape card is refined to a distinct mixed-level direct-sum tensor M2⊕M2⊕M1⊕M1. PR1779 covers homogeneous rank-one batches, PR1866 constructs a different (3,1,1,1) rank-six tensor without a phase-A placement, and the adjacent active rank-2/rank-3 claim excludes rank-one children. This scope tests the missing (2,2,1,1) shape at actual chronological occurrences in both full selected traces.
bottleneck_link: The selected complex-side cost is a concave moment of child rank. Replacing rank mass 6 from two rank-2 and two rank-1 children by one rank-6 child can reduce that moment while preserving paid rank mass; the task card requires at least a 5% ceiling gain.
stop_rule: Enumerate all contiguous four-event windows in both exact pinned traces. Admit only rank multiset {1,1,2,2} with four distinct destination columns; select a maximum disjoint schedule. Waive every added source, gather, output, frame, hosting, precision and restoration expense. Stop if the resulting exact ceiling misses 1.05 times the selected baseline ceiling; do not extend this cycle to moved events or a new source word.
evidence: Both orientations contain 24,767 events, 28 eligible windows and a maximum of 13 disjoint (2,2,1,1)->6 fusions. The ideal profile is {1:2386,2:392,3:432,4:142,5:82,6:13,8:8}; its exact ceiling bracket is [212305837/125000000000,1698446697/1000000000000], below the five-percent target 3549113631/2000000000000. Even with all new interface charges zero, at least 126 such blocks are needed: 125 is strictly below and 126 strictly above the target. Rank mass remains 5586. No physical supplier or kappa is claimed.
